messages:
nora: flagging an incident: a subset of eu-west edge proxies started failing mutual TLS handshakes ~09:00 UTC. affected pods log `failed to decrypt keystore blob: permission denied` and clients see TLS alert handshake_failure.

michael: which component is trying to decrypt? the tls-manager or the proxy sidecar?

nora: tls-manager (svc-tls-manager@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com) is responsible for fetching and decrypting per-tenant keystores from KMS-encrypted blobs in GCS. stacktrace excerpt: `tls-manager error: failed to open keystore: kms.Decrypt error: googleapi: Error 403: Permission denied to decrypt`

li: i deployed an RBAC tighten yesterday to remove roles/cloudkms.admin on a few infra SAs and replaced with key-scoped bindings. looks like tls-manager lost cryptoKeyDecrypter on the specific key used for eu-west keystores.

sec-bot: (audit) iam.policy_change detected: user li removed roles/cloudkms.admin from member serviceAccount:svc-tls-manager@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com at 1744996400

ana: quick note: we also noticed KMS DATA_ACCESS audit events for eu-west are not being forwarded to our SIEM because the org-level audit filter excludes DATA_ACCESS for KMS. makes it harder to confirm whether any decrypts succeeded before the deny.

michael: impact: customers using tenant TLS in eu-west experienced request failures and fallback to http2-plain for a small percentage; no keys appear leaked. initial hypothesis: config-only RBAC removal.

nora: mitigation plan i ran: 1) grant roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter on the eu-west keystore key to svc-tls-manager via key-level IAM 2) restart tls-manager pods in infra-eu-west 3) validate canary tenant handshake. commands i used: `gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding eu-west-keystore-key --location=global --keyring=prod-keys --member=serviceAccount:svc-tls-manager@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` and `kubectl -n infra-eu-west rollout restart deployment/tls-manager`

li: thanks, i'm patching the RBAC recipe to add an automated check in the PR job that runs `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy eu-west-keystore-key | grep svc-tls-manager` and fails if missing.

sec-bot: (audit) policy_update detected: org policy updated to include DATA_ACCESS forwarding for //cloudkms.googleapis.com/projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/prod-keys at 1745001200

ana: follow-ups: 1) confirm SIEM ingestion of KMS DATA_ACCESS for the window 08:50-09:20 UTC 2) add a canary that performs tenant keystore decrypt on every RBAC change 3) document least-privilege bindings for tls-manager (key-scoped) and include exact commands for emergency rollback 4) consider adding an RBAC change pre-merge checklist item to ping security for any KMS role changes

michael: vulnerability triage: no evidence of external compromise or key export. because decrypts were denied, we likely avoided accidental exposure. still running a deeper scan of audit logs once DATA_ACCESS is flowing.

nora: i'm preparing a short incident summary to share on the ops channel and will propose the postmortem if impact > 20m. initial outage window ~28 minutes from first error to confirmed canary success.

li: apologies for the disruption. i'll open PR to revert the stricter change and replace with key-scoped minimal binding. will include the CI check and a note to contact security before KMS role removals.

sec-bot: (note) incident-created id: INC-2026-0421-17 recorded at 1745003000

ana: adding one more hardening suggestion: add an integration test that validates TLS handshake for all regions after agent restarts; run it as part of infra-oncall daily checks.

michael: agreed. thanks everyone for the fast response.

nora: filing runbook edits and commands: https://runbooks.company/incidents/tls-keystore-authorization-fix (draft) :page_with_curl:
